territorial_scope.description: Applies to New Zealand agencies wherever they act, to overseas agencies acting in the course of carrying on business in New Zealand, and to certain non-resident individuals in relation to personal information they collected or held while present in New Zealand.

evidence.quote: an overseas agency (B), in relation to any action taken by B in the course of carrying on business in New Zealand

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: The Privacy Act 2020 regulates how New Zealand and overseas agencies handle personal information, through information privacy principles, complaints and investigations, breach notification and compliance notices. Most provisions commenced on 1 December 2020.
summary.long: The Privacy Act 2020 sets a framework for protecting individual privacy of personal information. It applies to New Zealand agencies, overseas agencies carrying on business in New Zealand, and certain individuals not ordinarily resident there. Its core is the information privacy principles (IPPs) in s 22, plus IPP 3A, which govern collection, source and notice, storage and security, access and correction, accuracy, retention, use and disclosure, disclosure outside New Zealand, and unique identifiers. The Privacy Commissioner may issue codes of practice that modify the IPPs. Individuals may request access to and correction of their personal information, and agencies may impose charges in limited cases. Complaints go to the Commissioner, who investigates and may refer matters to the Human Rights Review Tribunal, which can grant declarations, orders and damages. Agencies must notify the Commissioner and affected individuals of notifiable privacy breaches, and failing to notify the Commissioner is an offence with a fine not exceeding $10,000. The Commissioner may issue compliance notices. Part 7 authorises approved information sharing agreements and information matching. Part 8 restricts onward transfer outside New Zealand of personal information received from overseas, with transfer prohibition notices. Commencement was 1 December 2020, with IPP 3A from 1 May 2026.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the text from the title through section 138 (Part 7, subpart 1 interpretation). Parts 7 subparts 2 to 4, Parts 8 and 9, sections 213 to 218 and the Schedules are in part 2 and are not annotated here. Version as at 1 May 2026, a PCO consolidation with editorial changes; amendment history notes are treated as text evidence. Repeal of the Privacy Act 1993 is in s 216 (part 2) and is not coded here. Compare notes cite 1993 No 28 as the source of provisions and are not coded as relations. Commencement: the rest of the Act commences 1 December 2020 (s 2(2)); IPP 3A and s 25A have effect from 1 May 2026 per history notes. Relation target_instrument_id is empty where the target is not in the registry. Section status is not_applicable only because the schema requires it; the relations entries above are the annotation. Part 2 covers ss 139–216, Schedules 1–9 and the consolidation notes. Relations are those stated in this part only. Targets have no registry IDs, so target_instrument_id is blank and targets are identified by name. Amendment lines in the consolidation notes are coded as amended_by even where the affected provision is not identified. Compare references to the 1993 Act are not coded as separate relations. Schedule 5 lists information matching provisions in many other enactments; only the most relevant are coded above. Reader points: adverse-action notice periods differ (10 working days in s 152; 5 working days in s 181). Schedule 8 contains bracketed editorial text. Schedule 1 Part 2 applies from 1 May 2026.

thresholds.variable_text: individual under the age of 16 years (concerned individual)
thresholds.value_text: the individual concerned who is under the age of 16 years
thresholds.consequence: Agency may refuse access to personal information where disclosure would be contrary to the interests of the individual concerned who is under 16.
thresholds.conditions: Agency must consider that disclosure would be contrary to the interests of the under-16 individual concerned.

evidence.quote: the individual concerned who is under the age of 16 years

thresholds.variable_text: another individual to whom the information relates, under the age of 16 years
thresholds.value_text: another individual to whom the information relates who is under the age of 16 years
thresholds.consequence: Agency may refuse access to personal information where disclosure would be contrary to the interests of another under-16 individual to whom the information relates.
thresholds.conditions: Agency must consider that disclosure would be contrary to the interests of the under-16 individual.

evidence.quote: another individual to whom the information relates who is under the age of 16 years

thresholds.variable_text: affected individual under the age of 16
thresholds.value_text: if the individual is under the age of 16 and the agency believes that the notification or notice would be contrary to that individual’s interests
thresholds.consequence: Agency is not required to notify the under-16 affected individual or give public notice relating to that individual of a notifiable privacy breach; agency must consider notifying a representative instead.
thresholds.conditions: Agency believes that the notification or notice would be contrary to that individual’s interests.

evidence.quote: if the individual is under the age of 16 and the agency believes that the notification or notice would be contrary to that individual’s interests

thresholds.variable_text: affected individual under the age of 16 (representative)
thresholds.value_text: of an affected individual under the age of 16, means that individual’s parent or guardian
thresholds.consequence: For an affected individual under 16, the representative for notification purposes is that individual's parent or guardian.
thresholds.conditions: Applies where a representative is notified under s 116(3).

evidence.quote: of an affected individual under the age of 16, means that individual’s parent or guardian

thresholds.value_text: of an affected individual aged 16 or over, means an individual appearing to be lawfully acting on that individual’s behalf or in that individual’s interests
thresholds.consequence: For an affected individual aged 16 or over, the representative for notification purposes is an individual appearing to be lawfully acting on that individual's behalf or interests.
thresholds.conditions: Applies where a representative is notified under s 116(3).

evidence.quote: of an affected individual aged 16 or over, means an individual appearing to be lawfully acting on that individual’s behalf or in that individual’s interests

thresholds.variable_text: personal information about 10 or more individuals
thresholds.value_text: personal information about 10 or more individuals
thresholds.measurement: Counted per document: each of the two compared document sets must contain personal information about at least this many individuals.
thresholds.consequence: A comparison of documents meets the definition of information matching programme only at or above this count, which brings the programme within subpart 4 of Part 7.
thresholds.conditions: The comparison is for producing or verifying information that may be used for taking adverse action against an identifiable individual.

evidence.quote: any document that contains personal information about 10 or more individuals with 1 or more other documents that contain personal information about 10 or more individuals

thresholds.variable_text: persons over 14 years but under 18 years
thresholds.value_text: persons over 14 years but under 18 years
thresholds.measurement: Age of the person whose details of hearings are held in court records.
thresholds.consequence: Police, Serious Fraud Office and Legal Services Commissioner access to details of hearings is limited so as to exclude details relating to persons in this age band.
thresholds.conditions: Applies only where the offence did not carry a liability to imprisonment.

evidence.quote: access is limited so as to exclude details relating to young persons, being persons over 14 years but under 18 years, where the offence did not carry a liability to imprisonment

thresholds.measurement: Age of the person against whom Police proceedings were commenced before the commencement day.
thresholds.consequence: Transitional: Schedule 5 of the Privacy Act 1993 continues in force for Police access to the court record item relating to that person until the proceedings are discontinued or completed, sentencing is completed, and the outcome is recorded.
thresholds.conditions: Police commenced proceedings before the commencement day and those proceedings are not completed, or sentencing is pending; Police are accessing or intend to access details of hearings.

evidence.quote: the Police have commenced proceedings against a person aged 17 years, but those proceedings have not been completed, or, in respect of those proceedings, sentencing is pending
